Sample.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/13] Ten people participated in the study after having been informed and requested by specialists in psychology at three places of emergency psychiatry and by crisis resolution teams.

Population.evidence_source: [/page/1/Text/13] The interview subject must (i) have been considered seriously suicidal, but in the event of a suicide attempt, the interview should take place no earlier than 2 weeks afterwards, (ii) not be psychotic, (iii) be able to verbalize his/her experiences and (iv) have access to a therapist at least 2 weeks after the interview. The participants consisted of four women, aged from 21 to 45 years, and six men, aged from 25 to 52 years. Nine had made suicidal attempts prior to the interview, and one of them had tried four times during the previous month. Four persons had made one or more attempts in the past. Suicide was attempted by pills or substances. Five persons told about consumption of alcohol in advance of, or while taking, the pills. One person interviewed had not attempted suicide, but was prevented from carrying out a carefully planned suicide only by being involuntarily hospitalized.
